To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) cells produce tension in the ECM that is required to build up a long-range tissue organization; and (ii) the build-up of long-range organization enables a gradual conversion from cellular tension to pre-stressing the ECM.
the organization of the ECM in osteoid-like tissues can be explained by a combination of cellular tension and the pre-straining of ECM fibrils by neighbouring ECM fibrils.
the ECM is pre-stressed by cell-generated forces, and that cells can gradually convert cellular stress patterns into the pre-stress of the ECM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mechanical forces for the assembly of the ECM during tissue formation.
the development of the ECM in osteoid, which is a fundamental process for the development of healthy bone.
the role of cell-generated tension for the organization of the ECM during in vitro tissue generation and the resulting mechanical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ECM architecture is not only a consequence of cell-generated tension, but rather the outcome of a complex interaction between cells and the ECM.
the gradual build-up of a pre-stress in the ECM during tissue growth enables the maintenance of tissue tension in the absence of cell contraction.
the ECM fibrils act as pre-stresses, which are gradually converted into a pre-stressed matrix by cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell-generated tension is not sufficient to produce a pre-stressed ECM architecture, but it is necessary.
cells are the main drivers for ECM organization in tissues, but that the ECM also contributes to the maintenance of the tissue architecture.
cells and ECM form an interdependent system that allows cells to maintain a constant level of tension, while the ECM is progressively pre-stressed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell-generated tension and ECM fibril organization are not mutually exclusive but rather mutually reinforcing, and that a cell-organized ECM can be a source for pre-stress in tissues.
cell-generated tension is a crucial driving force in the development of the ECM and its long-range organization.
the organization of cells and fibrils is not only important to maintain tissue homeostasis, it also plays a crucial role in the development of tissue organization.
